title: add reproducible RAG quickstart with seeded indexing and inline evals
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: engineers repeatedly asked for a RAG quickstart that guarantees deterministic CI runs for regression tests and reproducible authoring iterations. This PR adds a compact reproducible RAG starter that includes a seeded indexer, deterministic model sandbox settings, an inline evaluation harness with golden prompt sets, and CI smoke tests to validate rank/recall and deterministic output tokens. Contents: quickstarts/reproducible-rag README with step-by-step onboarding; seeded_indexer (Python) that stores deterministic sharded indices; example prompt/ground-truth bundle for inline evals; a lightweight Dockerfile and CI workflow that runs smoke e2e with seeded RNG and cached vector DB; a minimal TypeScript sample showing tool-calling and structured output validation. Checklist: [x] Add README and quickstart materials; [x] Implement seeded indexer and deterministic seeding flags; [x] Add example prompt set and expected hashes; [x] Add CI workflow that runs smoke tests and fails on nondeterminism; [x] Add short tutorial paragraph for using with Redwood Console evals. Usage highlights: developers can run `make dev-up` to launch a seeded local index and then run the eval harness `scripts/run_eval.sh --seed 42` which asserts token-level stable outputs for the golden prompts; CI uses the same flags. Backwards compatibility: this is purely additive to quickstarts, uses feature flags and does not change any runtime. Related work: ENG-1423 (reproducible-evals), DOC-88 (quickstart refresh). Notes: examples use a lightweight in-memory vector store shim for fast CI, and the README explains tradeoffs for production indices and privacy considerations.
